title: AC Store — Acceptance Criterion YAML Schema
description: JSON Schema (draft-07) for acceptance criterion files stored under docs/acceptance-criteria/. See ADR-008 for rationale and ID format specification.

id.description: Stable AC identifier. Supports multiple formats: base form PREFIX-NNN (e.g. ACS-100, FIN-001), hierarchical L1 form PREFIX-NNNx (e.g. ACS-100a), L2 form PREFIX-NNNx-N (e.g. ACS-500a-1), L3 extension form PREFIX-NNNx-N-y (e.g. ACS-500a-1-i), numeric-only hierarchy (e.g. BO-510-1), and compound-prefix forms (e.g. KM-DBF-001). Assigned at creation time; never changes.

title.description: One-line human-readable description of the criterion.

component.description: Component name matching a key in docs/acceptance-criteria/index.yaml.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the criterion. 'superseded' (without _by) is an alternate form used by some older records; 'superseded_by' is the canonical form for new records.

criteria.description: Multi-line Gherkin scenario body (Given/When/Then/And). When implements_pattern is set and the AC has no unique behavior beyond what the pattern provides, a plain-text placeholder is acceptable (e.g. 'No page-specific behavior — all behavior inherited from pattern.').

created_by.description: Path to the ticket (relative to repo root) that first introduced this criterion. Used by some authoring flows (newer records use 'created' for the date and 'created_by_ticket' for the ticket path).

created.description: Date this AC was created. Stored as a YAML date (YYYY-MM-DD). YAML parsers deserialise bare YYYY-MM-DD values as native date objects; the schema intentionally accepts any non-null scalar (string or date) to accommodate both quoted and unquoted YAML date syntax.

created_by_ticket.description: Path to the ticket (relative to repo root) that introduced this criterion. Used by newer authoring flows alongside 'created'.

superseded_by.description: AC ID (or list of AC IDs when split into multiple successors) of the replacement criterion. Set when status is superseded_by. Null when not superseded. A list form occurs when an AC is split into two or more successor ACs.

amended_by.description: Ticket paths, free-form amendment notes, or structured amendment records that subsequently amended this criterion. Items may be plain strings (ticket paths or freeform notes) or objects with a 'reason' key (structured amendment records produced by agent workflows).

covered_by.description: Test file paths (optionally with ::test_function), child AC IDs, or other references that verify or cover this criterion.

implemented_by.description: Source file paths (optionally with #anchor) that implement this criterion.

origin_agent.description: Identity of the agent or workflow that created this AC file. Free-form provenance string — any non-empty value is valid. Historical agent names (e.g. business-analyst-v2, business-analyst-v3, create-ticket, refinement from now-deleted or renamed agents) remain valid and are never rewritten.

readiness.description: Lifecycle readiness state of this AC. draft = written but not reviewed (scanner ignores); reviewed = IT PO v3 has enriched and approved (scanner ignores); approved = user has signed off (scanner may pick up).

priority.description: Implementation priority of this AC. Set by the user (or PO v3) at approval time. Used by the scanner for ranking.

documentation_triggers.description: List of documentation types that must be produced for this feature. Valid on L1 ACs only. Set by product-owner-v3 based on the nature of the feature. Empty array means no docs needed (provide documentation_rationale in that case).

documentation_rationale.description: Required when documentation_triggers is empty on an L1 AC. Explains why no documentation is needed.

oneOf.description: Implementation lifecycle status for this AC. not_started/todo = not yet implemented; in_progress = implementation underway; done = implemented and verified. 'not_started' is an alternate form of 'todo' used by some older records.

Hierarchy level of this AC. L0 = top-level composite (portfolio/program); L1 = composite (epic/feature); L2 = implementable leaf (story/task); L3 = fine-grained implementable leaf (sub-task). L0/L1 ACs are composite — fulfillment is derived from children, not directly verified.

List of AC IDs that this AC depends on. Used for parent-child hierarchy links (child AC lists its structural parent) and for pattern composition (composite pattern lists its atomic component pattern IDs). Must not form a cycle — the check_ac_circular_deps pre-commit hook enforces a directed-acyclic-graph (DAG) invariant on all depends_on edges.

ID of the reusable behavior pattern this AC inherits from (e.g. 'PTN-001'). When set, the effective behavior is derived from the referenced pattern combined with any pattern_bindings. The criteria field may contain a plain-text placeholder rather than a full Given/When/Then scenario.
Key-value bindings that instantiate the referenced pattern for this AC. Values may be strings, arrays, or objects. Only meaningful when implements_pattern is set.

List of {word} placeholder strings that this pattern AC exposes as bindable slots. Only meaningful on pattern ACs (ACs that other ACs reference via implements_pattern). Each entry is a placeholder in the form '{slot_name}' matching a named placeholder in the criteria field. Consuming ACs must supply a value for every slot via pattern_bindings.

assigned_agent.description: Name of the implementation agent (e.g. 'python-coder', 'sql-coder') assigned to implement this AC. Null when unassigned.

estimated_complexity.description: T-shirt size complexity estimate for implementing this AC. Set by it-po during technical enrichment. Valid values: XS, S, M, L, XL.

delivers_to.description: Contract describing what this AC's implementation delivers to a downstream agent or consumer. May be null (no downstream contract), a free-form string agent name, a structured object {agent, contract}, or a list of such objects.

expects_from.description: Contract describing what this AC expects to receive from an upstream agent or dependency. May be null (no upstream contract), a free-form string AC ID, a structured object {agent, contract}, or a list of such objects.

package_surface.description: Explicit declaration that this AC registers a PACKAGE SURFACE — an entry in a registry the build reads to decide what a consumer project receives (config/agent_registry.json, config/skill_registry.json, config/paths.json, templates/scripts/commit_guardian/commit_guardian.json). Set it to true, deliberately, when the AC's work brings such a surface into existence. This declaration is the SOLE trigger for the structured it_requirements obligation below (ACS-100i-6): the obligation is no longer inferred from assigned_agent or from how the AC spells its component, because that proxy both over-matched (243 of the store's 280 refusals were records registering no config key at all) and under-matched (440 records spelling the namespace 'build-pipeline' were invisible to it). Absent or false means no structured implementation spec is demanded, whatever the AC's agent, component or components values. Registering a surface without declaring it here is caught at landing time by the check-package-surface-declaration commit hook (ACS-100i-8), which reconciles the registry entries a change actually adds against the declarations of the ACs it cites.

it_requirements.description: Technical requirements for implementing this AC. May be a multi-line string, a list of requirement strings, or — for ACs declaring `package_surface: true` — a structured object with machine-checkable implementation fields (config_schema_fragment, reference_file_path, n_location_rule, required_skills, post_write_commands). Set by it-po during technical enrichment. NOTE: whenever the object form is used it is held to ALL five fields by the object branch below, independently of the package_surface declaration (ACS-100i-6-i) — narrowing the trigger must never become a way to file a half-populated structured spec.

oneOf.description: Structured implementation spec required for ACs declaring `package_surface: true`. Must include all five required implementation fields. This branch's `required` list is enforced for EVERY record that uses the object form, declared or not — see ACS-100i-6-i.

config_schema_fragment.description: JSON Schema fragment describing the config key this AC registers (object or any valid schema type).

reference_file_path.description: Path (relative to repo root) to the file that must be modified for registration. Must be a real, resolvable path — validated at authoring time by validate_ac.py.

n_location_rule.description: How many locations in reference_file_path must be updated (e.g. '1', 'all', 'one per component'). Prevents partial-registration defects.

required_skills.description: List of skills or agent names required to implement this AC (e.g. ['python-coder', 'knowledge-query']).

post_write_commands.description: Commands to run after modifying the reference file (e.g. ['python scripts/build.py']). May be empty for ACs that require no build step.

test_spec.description: Source-of-truth test contract for this AC. The AC — not the ticket — owns what must be tested. A list of test-stub descriptors that test-writer authors as failing tests, and that generate_ticket_from_ac.py derives the ticket's ## Test Requirements section from (parallel to it_requirements -> ## Implementation Notes). Set by it-po during technical enrichment on L2/L3 code ACs. Null/absent means 'no test contract authored yet'; an empty list is not permitted (use test_required: false for genuinely test-free ACs).

name.description: Test function or class name (e.g. test_merged_output_sorted_by_priority). Should be descriptive enough to read as an assertion.

target_dir.description: Repo-relative directory the test file lives in (e.g. unit_tests/ac_store/).

framework.description: Test framework. Defaults to the project convention (unittest) when omitted.

type.description: Test level. Guides where the test runs and how heavy its fixtures are.

angle.description: Which proof-of-done question this test answers, from the set-cover taxonomy in docs/testing/test-angles.md — five core angles (criterion, reachability, seam, real_artifact, deployed) plus two conditional ones (boundary, failure). Authoring it here is how an it-po declares that this test already covers a given angle: generate_ticket_from_ac.py passes the value straight through onto the ticket's ## Test Requirements entry. Note the criteria-derived fallback (used when no test_spec is authored) tags its own descriptors 'criterion' and appends one mandatory 'reachability' descriptor; an authored test_spec that already carries one 'reachability'-angle entry keeps it unaltered and gains no second one (BO-2900g-1-i). Omit when the angle has not been classified.

surface_invoked.description: BO-2900g-3: the entry-point field, carried under the name the (now-retired) ticket-facing definition already used. Names the CLI, hook script, slash command, or agent entrypoint a reachability-kind test must actually invoke, or holds the single 'entry point is not declared' sentinel when nothing upstream named one. Optional here — the generator's own reachability descriptor states the same fact via its 'asserts' field (BO-2900g-1-i) when this is omitted.

description.description: One sentence: what this test asserts. Maps to a Gherkin Then clause in criteria.

covers.description: AC IDs this test covers. Defaults to [this AC's id] when omitted.

requires_db.description: Whether the test needs a live database (drives slow-test marking).

test_required.description: Whether test-writer must produce failing tests for this AC. Distinguishes 'intentionally no tests' (false — e.g. change_target prompt/docs) from 'test contract not yet authored' (null/absent). Defaults to true for code/schema ACs. When false, test-writer skips with an accurate, non-hardcoded reason instead of misclassifying the AC as docs-only.

test_rationale.description: Prose justification for the test contract in test_spec: why this shape of coverage is the right one, and why a weaker shape (typically a direct-import unit test) would be insufficient for this AC. Must be a string, never a list. Absent or null when no rationale has been authored.

doc_links.description: Documentation links related to this AC. Each item is either a plain file-path string or an object with path, relationship, status, and optional relevance fields.

path.description: Relative path to the linked document.

relationship.description: How this document relates to the AC (e.g. 'describes', 'specifies', 'implements').

status.description: Existence status of the linked document.

relevance.description: Optional free-form note on why this document is relevant.

req_status.description: Requirement lifecycle status. Tracks whether the requirement is still active from a product perspective (independent of implementation work_status).

roadmap_phase.description: Roadmap phase this AC belongs to (e.g. 'phase_1'). Matches a phase key in docs/roadmap.json.

target_epic.description: Name of the epic folder this AC's generated ticket was assembled into (e.g. 'EPIC-TrustThatAGreenCheckActuallyChecked'). Written by scripts/goal_to_epic.py, which reads it back on a re-run to decide whether the AC already belongs to an epic. Absent until an epic has been generated from the AC.

notes.description: Free-form contextual notes about this AC — authorship context, post-implementation findings, or rationale that does not belong in criteria.

parent.description: Explicit parent AC ID. Used when the structural parent cannot be mechanically derived from the ID format (e.g. non-standard ID hierarchies). Prefer the id-based derivation algorithm where possible.

components.description: Authoritative component-membership list — the field the knowledge graph reads to build component_membership edges (config/paths.json 'acs' surface edge_fields), so it must be present and non-empty. Every value must be a component id declared in docs/components.json (the single canonical component registry, shared with the docs surface via check_doc_frontmatter). The scalar 'component' is a SEPARATE axis: it is the AC-store namespace/prefix key from docs/acceptance-criteria/index.yaml (kebab) used for AC id generation and file placement, and is intentionally NOT migrated to this vocabulary. Keep this enum in sync with docs/components.json keys.

scope.description: Scope qualifier for this AC (e.g. 'standing' for standing/permanent requirements that persist across sprints).

child_limit_override.description: Per-parent override that raises (never lowers) the default child count hard cap for this specific AC. When set to an integer N, the check-ac-tree-limits hook uses max(default_cap, N) as the effective cap for this parent. An override below the default cap is silently ignored (fail-open). An OVERRIDE ACTIVE audit line is emitted to stderr when the override is active and child_count exceeds the default. This field is a temporary, audited escape hatch -- it should be removed once the structural reorganisation (e.g. AC-UID-decoupling) is complete. Only meaningful on L0 and L1 ACs (the only levels with a child hard cap).

change_target.description: Classification of what kind of artifact this AC targets. Used by the computed quality-gates pipeline to look up mandatory guardrail agents. Accepts either a single value (string) or a list of values (array of strings). Enum is the ADR-017 blast-radius vocabulary: 10 canonical change-target labels. Optional — absent when the AC predates the computed-gates pipeline (ticket 10 will backfill).

risk_surface.description: Classification of the blast-radius / risk exposure of this AC. Used by the computed quality-gates pipeline alongside change_target to select mandatory guardrail agents. Enum is the ADR-017 blast-radius vocabulary: 6 canonical risk-surface labels. Optional — absent when the AC predates the computed-gates pipeline (ticket 10 will backfill).

declares_side_effect.description: Declares that this AC's work produces a durable, observable side-effect on a user-facing surface (a file written, a record persisted, a command that changes state) rather than only returning a value. Authored by it-po (or business-analyst) during enrichment; set it to true whenever the AC's Then clause asserts something observable outside the process. Effect: generate_ticket_from_ac.py reads this field and automatically routes the user-surface-smoker phase agent into the generated ticket's agents map as 'needed', and propagates declares_side_effect: true to the ticket frontmatter (BP-1100f-5). The gate is NON-OVERRIDABLE — an explicit user-surface-smoker: not_needed override is ignored while this field is true (BP-1100f-5, mirroring the BO-550-1-i protection for the TDD agents). Absence (or false/null) means the AC makes no durable side-effect claim and is NOT force-routed to the smoker (BP-1100f-5-i); the exemption is data-driven, never by item name. This is the repo's one automatic guard against 'the code was built but is not wired into anything'.

product_truth.description: TOOL-OWNED derived back-reference into the product-truth store (docs/product-truth/). GENERATED by docs/product-truth/scripts/generate_product_truth.py as the inversion of every flow step/branch whose `implements` list contains this AC id — NEVER hand-edited. The authored link direction is flow->AC (step.implements); this list is the recomputed reverse edge so an AC is self-describing (which flow nodes / screens / mock data realise it). The relationship is many-to-many, so this is a LIST. The key is omitted entirely when no flow node references this AC. Regenerate (do not edit) if it drifts; the product-truth validator errors on any mismatch against the by_ac inversion.

flow.description: id of the flow artifact (<product>/<name>) whose node references this AC.

node.description: id of the step or branch within the flow that carries this AC in its `implements` list.

node_kind.description: Whether the referencing node is a flow step or a branch.

flow_kind.description: The referencing flow's kind (user | data | architecture).

screen.description: Bare mockup screen id this node renders, or null when the node has no screen.

mock_data.description: id of the flow's mock_data_ref dataset, or null when the flow has none.

entities.description: Sorted, de-duplicated entity names the node reads/writes.

asof.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) this back-reference was last regenerated.

if.description: Package-surface AC detection (ACS-100i-6): applies when, and only when, the record explicitly declares `package_surface: true`. Neither assigned_agent nor component (nor components) is consulted — a package surface can be registered from any namespace by any agent, and how a record spells its component must never change this verdict (ACS-100i-6-ii).

then.description: For records declaring a package surface, it_requirements MUST be a structured object (not a plain string, an array or null) with the five required implementation fields. This prevents fictional or thin specs from reaching the coder.
